headline: President Biden ended the national emergency concerning Zimbabwe that had been in place since 2003.
what_it_does: This executive order ends a national emergency the US government had declared over the situation in Zimbabwe. National emergencies like this one are usually the legal basis for economic sanctions, such as freezing assets and blocking business dealings. Ending the emergency generally ends the sanctions program built on it. The title alone does not say whether any other measures replaced it.

who_it_affects.group: People and companies in Zimbabwe who were under US sanctions
who_it_affects.how: Sanctions tied to this emergency would generally no longer apply to them.
Rules that limited their dealings with people and groups named under the Zimbabwe sanctions program would generally be lifted.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed March 4, 2024; the exact effective date is not stated in the source provided.
